title: Folding and Enfolding Walls: Statist Imperatives and Bureaucratic Aesthetics in Divided Jerusalem
thesis: The paper analyzes a vector of wall-like architectural forms in Jerusalem as a topological mechanism of statist control, folding and enfolding space to reinforce state imperatives and destroy Palestinian urban life.
theme_1_justification: Not addressed. The paper focuses on physical walls and architecture, not on software/data properties or dual-use technology transfer.
theme_2_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of algorithmic opacity, epistemic authority of data, or surveillance as knowledge production. The paper uses aesthetic and topological analysis, not data-driven governance.
theme_3_justification: Not addressed. Although the paper discusses control and modulation through Deleuzian folding, it is about physical architectural forms (walls, museum, mall, barrier), not algorithmic governance, smart cities, or data-driven urban management.
theme_4_justification: Central argument. The paper extensively discusses spatial destruction through the separation barrier, home unmaking of Palestinians (e.g., tens of thousands cut off from services), the mall-wall as a battering ram driving into the Old City, and the weaponization of urban space. The vector culminates in the brutal security barrier that blocks and destroys Palestinian metropolitan Jerusalem.
key_quotes: The effect of the security barrier will be to destroy Palestinian metropolitan Jerusalem 'and control it without annexing it' (Klein 2005: 71).

Up close, it is a row of huge blunt teeth sunk into the earth, their bite savage and unyielding. Horizons of living are blocked, perspective severely foreshortened. One cannot look over, under, or around.

Beginning with the harmonic pylon-parabola as the entry to the historic and holy capital, gathering sacrificial empowerment through the museum-wall, its velocity becoming more directional, the vector accelerates through the mall-wall, gathering the power to own and fetishize, pinning Palestinians-as-objects against the security barrier with Holocaust history, squeezing, flattening, and sacrificing them with the power to consume against its unyielding, brute form.
policy_relevance: None. The paper critiques existing state practices but does not offer policy recommendations.
notes: Paper is about physical architecture and spatial control in Jerusalem, not algorithmic governance or dual-use software/data. Scores reflect low direct relevance to the SLR's core themes, except Theme 4 which is strongly addressed.
